guides.title: Reading difficulties
guides.concern: A learner often reads words differently from what is written.
observable_behaviours: Reads a different vowel sound (hat as hit).
Leaves off word endings (dig for digs).
Skips small words or whole lines.
context_questions: Does this happen with unfamiliar words or with all words?
Is the learner reading in their home language?
Was the room noisy or was the learner tired?
alternative_explanations: The words or language are unfamiliar.
The print is small or the page is crowded.
The learner is tired, anxious, or distracted.
things_to_try_now: Try chunked text or sound-by-sound pointing from the support catalogue.
Pre-teach 3 to 4 hard words before reading.
Record a baseline with Form A and compare with a matched follow-up.
what_to_record: Which words were read differently, exactly as heard.
Whether the pattern repeats across two attempts.
What support was tried and for how long.
guides.how_to_judge: Compare words read as written on matched passages before and after the support, with the careful wording on the comparison screen.
guides.when_to_seek_help: If the pattern is sustained across attempts plus your observations, consider discussing it with a qualified professional.
guides.non_diagnostic_statement: MINDTRACE gives educational observations, not diagnoses.

guides.title: Attention and executive function
guides.concern: A learner struggles to start, stay with, or finish a task.
observable_behaviours: Loses their place or repeats steps.
Seems to forget the instruction midway.
context_questions: How long was the task, and how many steps did it have?
What time of day was it?
Did a shorter version go better?
alternative_explanations: The task was long or had many steps.
The learner was tired or hungry.
The instructions were given all at once.
The format did not suit them.
things_to_try_now: Give one step at a time with extra processing time.
Shorten the task and add a visible break.
Let the learner respond in a different format.
what_to_record: How long the learner stayed with the task, in minutes.
Which step they reached before stopping.
What changed when the task was shortened.
guides.how_to_judge: Compare completion on the same task shape before and after the change.
guides.when_to_seek_help: If difficulty persists across settings and strategies, consider discussing it with a qualified professional.
guides.non_diagnostic_statement: MINDTRACE gives educational observations, not diagnoses.

guides.title: Learning in a second or additional language
guides.concern: A learner who speaks another language at home makes consistent sound-pattern errors in English reading.
observable_behaviours: Substitutes sounds that do not exist in the home language.
Reads fluently in the home language but hesitates in English.
Understands the story when it is discussed but stumbles reading it.
context_questions: Which languages does the learner speak at home?
How long have they been learning in English?
Do the errors follow a consistent sound pattern?
alternative_explanations: The sound pattern is unfamiliar, not a reading barrier.
Vocabulary in the passage is new.
The learner has had less time with English print.
things_to_try_now: Pre-teach vocabulary with pictures before reading.
Use listen-then-read so the sounds are heard first.
Check understanding by discussion, not only by reading aloud.
what_to_record: Home language and time learning in English.
Whether discussion shows the content is understood.
guides.how_to_judge: Look for the pattern across attempts and check it against the home-language explanation first.
guides.when_to_seek_help: If difficulty persists in all languages the learner uses, consider discussing it with a qualified professional.
guides.non_diagnostic_statement: MINDTRACE gives educational observations, not diagnoses.
